answer: In an agent marketplace, ridge, cedar, and echo must each lock 100 tokens in a separate on-chain bond before bidding for work. The contract prevents the same tokens from backing multiple identities and holds each bond for 30 days after its agent exits. An attacker creating 1,000 fake agents therefore needs 100,000 tokens tied up for at least a month, making identities costly in capital even when generating new keys is free.
